paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: knowing God is not about what you do on the calendar. Paul says the Galatians used to be slaves to those who by nature are not gods, but now they know God, or rather, are known by God (Galatians 4:8-9). So why go back to "weak and worthless principles" and pile up special days and months and seasons and years (Galatians 4:9-10)? Being known by God is the whole prize, and you can't earn a prize that's already in your hands!

Second, real love tells you the truth, even when it stings. Paul asks, "Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?" (Galatians 4:16). Then he says those other people are zealous for the Galatians, but not in a good way, because they want to isolate them (Galatians 4:17). I think the difference is easy to spot, baker: somebody who loves you wants you close to Christ, and somebody who just wants a crowd wants you close to THEM.

Third, look at how Paul feels about all this. He fears his efforts may have been in vain, he's perplexed, and he says he is again in the pains of childbirth "until Christ is formed in you" (Galatians 4:19-20). I bet he has not stopped hoping, because that's what a father does. So if you ever feel like you've drifted, friend, hear the same thing I did from that angel when I was stuck in a drawer: you haven't been forgotten. Come on back to Christ, and let Him keep shaping you.
